claims.text: On 2026-08-14 the clinician recorded INR 3.8 and advised reducing warfarin to 2.5 mg nightly with an INR recheck on Friday.

citations.quote: INR 3.8. Reduce warfarin 2.5 mg nightly and recheck INR on Friday.

claims.text: Patient reports on 2026-08-16 still taking warfarin 5 mg every night, which conflicts with the documented 2.5 mg nightly dose.

citations.quote: I am still taking warfarin 5 mg every night like before.

claims.text: The record contains a dose conflict for warfarin: 2.5 mg in the clinician note versus 5 mg in the patient note.

open_questions: When was warfarin first recorded, and what doses have been documented over time? Only the 2026-08-14 and 2026-08-16 entries are present.
What was the INR trend before the 3.8 on 2026-08-14? No earlier INR values appear in the record.
Has the warfarin dose reduction ordered on 2026-08-14 been acknowledged or acted on? The later patient note indicates 5 mg is still being taken.
Was the Friday INR recheck performed, and what was the result? No result is recorded.
What was the indication for warfarin, and are there prior bleeding or thrombotic events on record? Neither is documented.
How long has the patient been self-reporting 5 mg nightly, and was the dose change discussed with the patient? The record does not say.
Are any allergies or reactions recorded? None appear in the record.
Are any other follow-ups, referrals or tests planned besides the INR recheck? None are documented.

candidate_highlights.risk_reason: Patient reports taking warfarin 5 mg nightly two days after a clinician note advising 2.5 mg nightly, a dose conflict with possible bleeding risk after INR 3.8.
candidate_highlights.suggested_action: Have the clinician confirm the intended warfarin dose and that the dose change was communicated to the patient.

candidate_highlights.risk_reason: INR 3.8 above range and the ordered Friday INR recheck has no recorded result.
